Article Title: CBSE makes AI a part of formal teaching, NCERT develops module
Article Text:
NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII, which CBSE has earmarked for school-based assessment.

NEW DELHI: From spotting deepfake to questioning a chatbot’s confident but incorrect answers, artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from being an optional subject towards becoming a basic skill for CBSE schoolchildren. Taking a step towards more formal AI teaching in schools, NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII, which it has earmarked for school-based assessment. Separate AI textbooks are also being prepared for students pursuing the subject at a more advanced level.The move is part of a wider effort to make AI literacy accessible to students, irrespective of whether they study computers or choose AI as an elective. The idea is to first familiarise children with how the technology works, its uses and limitations, before moving towards more structured teaching through textbooks.NCERT developed the module on computational thinking (CT) and AI in consultation with IIT Madras and IIT Jodhpur.In an April-9 circular, CBSE had announced that NCERT would provide modules for Classes IX-XII for internal assessment during the 2026-27 academic session.Under the board’s revised scheme, CT and AI modules are compulsory for Class IX, while Class X continues under the existing scheme.A senior education ministry official said AI had become an important part of everyday activities, from education and research to content writing and career guidance. “AI tools are being used for studies, research, content writing and even career advice. Students will be taught how to use AI tools correctly and fact-check information,” they said.
Article Summary: NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII. Separate AI textbooks are also being prepared for students pursuing the subject at a more advanced level. The idea is to familiarise children with how the technology works, its uses and limitations.

Article Title: In 2025, Lee and Don Cameron took a 12-month job as Low Isles’ live-in caretakers; their 7-day weeks start before 6 a.m. amid thousands of noisy birds
Article Text:
The Great Barrier Reef, which the Low Island is a part of | Wikimedia Commons

The birds are part of the job

Maintenance without a nearby hardware store

Low island, with the lighthouse visible | Wikimedia Commons

A seven-day working week

The Tasmanian couple took a 12-month contract as live-in caretakers of Low Island, part of the Great Barrier Reef, and traded a self-built off-grid home for a job that requires them to maintain buildings, manage vegetation and help protect the island’s natural environment. The couple’s appointment was announced by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority on October 29, 2025, which said that they had won a tender to replace outgoing caretakers Colin and Renata Musson. The role involves looking after heritage buildings and infrastructure, coordinating with tour operators, welcoming visitors and monitoring compliance with marine park rules..Low Island is about 15 kilometres northeast of Port Douglas, and along with nearby Woody Island, it forms the Low Isles group, a pair of coral cays that are surrounded by reef waters popular with snorkellers, researchers and tour groups. The area attracts about 50,000 visitors annually, according to the Marine Park Authority. The annual nesting season brought large numbers of bridled terns and pied imperial pigeons to the island, which is when the Camerons arrived, and in an October 28 report, ABC News described the noise from the birds as a constant feature of life there. Little terns tap along the island’s aluminium stairs, pigeons coo, and other seabirds produce louder calls through the night and early morning.Lee Cameron told ABC that she enjoyed observing the birds and their individual behaviour, even when the noise became difficult. The island’s wildlife is a part of the caretaking work, as the couple has experience with monitoring seabirds and other species through conservation volunteering in Tasmania.Caretakers must clean and repair heritage buildings, manage weeds, keep visitor areas presentable and maintain essential infrastructure, while also overseeing systems that support the island’s off-grid operation, including solar power, rainwater collection and filtration, wastewater treatment and composting toilets. The Marine Park Authority describes Low Island as a carbon-neutral coral cay, and its facilities have to keep working despite the island’s isolation, heat, humidity and exposure to cyclones. Supplies and specialist help are not as readily available as they would be on the mainland, so caretakers need practical maintenance skills and the ability to handle problems independently.The Camerons spent 12 years travelling internationally by sailboat before returning to Tasmania, where they built an off-grid solar home overlooking the River Derwent. They had also volunteered on several remote islands and worked on heritage lighthouse projects, and their previous experience included conservation work on Maatsuyker Island, where volunteers monitor wildlife in challenging conditions. The couple’s Low Isles contract also requires them to welcome visitors and liaise with tour operators, which means that the island is both a workplace and a destination used by day-trippers, even though the caretakers live there full-time.ABC News reported that the typical day begins before 6 a.m. and that the work continues seven days a week. Tasks vary, but can include raking, checking facilities, gardening, repairs and cleaning, and Lee said that the routine involved more walking than she had expected when she first saw the size of the island. The couple have a residence on Low Island, while separate accommodation is available for visiting researchers and volunteers. They can seek help with larger jobs that exceed what two caretakers can manage themselves, but ordinary upkeep remains their responsibility.
Article Summary: Tasmanian couple join Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority as live-in caretakers of Low Island. The job involves looking after heritage buildings and infrastructure, coordinating with tour operators, welcoming visitors and monitoring compliance with marine park rules. Low Island is about 15 kilometres northeast of Port Douglas, and along with nearby Woody Island, it forms the Low Isles group.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Text:
What sets the 3D periodic table apart

Google DeepMind has revealed a way to demonstrate the capabilities of its latest artificial intelligence (AI) system: a full chemistry visualisation synched to music. Using its recently launched Gemini 4 Argon model, DeepMind generated an interactive, three-dimensional periodic table that choreographs its movements to the tempo and lyrics of Tom Lehrer’s classic 1959 song, “The Elements. ” As the fast-paced tune plays, the visualisation highlights each element in real time, displaying animated electron pathways, detailed atomic specifications, and individual light spectra.The video was shared by Google Deepmind and re-shared by Google CEO Sundar Pichai, saying, “Sound on!”. The video surfaced a week after Gemini 4 Argon’s official public debut. In an amusing nod noted by observers, a model bearing the name of the noble gas Argon was used to reconstruct the periodic table itself.Built by DeepMind’s Antigravity development platform, the project moves well past the familiar flat grid of atomic symbols found in standard chemistry textbooks. The demonstration coordinates multiple layers of data and rendering simultaneously:Each element is rendered with moving electron orbits rather than flat diagrams, and the interface presents comprehensive atomic specifications alongside the specific light emission spectra for each material.Moreover, the most technically demanding element of the demo is its timing. Lehrer’s track is famous for rattling off element names at breakneck speed. Gemini 4 Argon successfully synchronized the visual rendering, underlying scientific datasets, and audio playback to hit each vocal cue and musical beat precisely.“Gemini 4 Argon built a 3D periodic table synced to Tom Lehrer’s song, “The Elements.” Created in @Antigravity, it animates orbiting electrons, atomic data, and light spectra,” Google DeepMind said.The periodic table is not an official benchmark score, instead, it serves as a creative demonstration of how the model handles complex, multi-stage "agentic" instructions that require synthesizing scientific logic, graphic generation, and real-time audio synchronization.Gemini 4 Argon rolled out publicly on October 13, 2026, with Google DeepMind targeting the system at sophisticated operational workflows, including scientific exploration and large-scale software engineering.
Article Summary: Gemini 4 Argon model synched to Tom Lehrer’s classic 1959 song, “The Elements. ” As the fast-paced tune plays, the visualisation highlights each element in real time, displaying animated electron pathways, detailed atomic specifications, and individual light spectra.

Article Title: Explained: How YouTube watching experience is set to improve with next-gen streaming technology
Article Text:
YouTube

YouTube’s rapid open-codec shift

Unlocking multi-view and richer browser experiences

YouTube is about to enhance its video streaming experience with an upcoming move to next-generation video compression technology that promises sharper visual quality while consuming comparatively less internet bandwidth. Earlier this year, the Alliance for Open Media finalised the official specifications for the AV2 codec. Engineering projections indicate that AV2 is roughly 25% to 32% more efficient than its predecessor, AV1. In practical terms, this efficiency gain allows platforms to stream noticeably higher-definition video at existing bitrates, or maintain sharp, pristine image clarity at significantly lower bitrates, essentially cutting down total data consumption for viewers.While major streaming peers such as Netflix, Amazon, and Apple have remained silent regarding their deployment roadmaps, YouTube is moving ahead openly. According to a report by Android Authority, YouTube has confirmed plans to begin rolling out AV2 streaming as early as early 2027, targeting the web browser version of the platform first.YouTube has anchored its infrastructure around royalty-free, open-standard compression technologies.“YouTube champions open codecs that deliver the best quality video with the fewest playback interruptions. As of March 19, 2026, over 90% of YouTube’s catalog (weighted by watch time) is available in AV1. And we’re excited to begin streaming in AV2, which brings even better video quality to users and unlocks new multi-video capabilities. YouTube AV2 streams will be available for Web as soon as early 2027,” Des Keane, Engineering Director at YouTube was quoted as saying.The performance leap delivered by AV2 extends past standard video playback. Engineering leadership at Google Chrome notes that the compression gains will enable complex layout features inside internet browsers.Jim Bankoski, engineering vice president of Chrome, highlighted the broader potential of the standard:“We’re encouraged by the momentum around AV2, with partners like YouTube, Netflix, and Prime Video exploring the format and showing strong support for the technology. Beyond faster, higher-quality streaming, AV2 lays the groundwork for new browser experiences, from better multi-view video to higher-resolution, more efficient video conferencing.”The multi-video capability could allow sports fans or event viewers to watch several high-definition camera feeds simultaneously on a single monitor without exhausting system resources or network capacity.However, despite YouTube’s timeline, widespread adoption of AV2 across everyday consumer electronics will take time.Historical rollouts show that video codec adoption moves slowly through global supply chains. For comparison, the original AV1 standard was finalised back in 2018, yet commercial smartphones featuring dedicated AV1 hardware encoding did not arrive on the market until the launch of the Google Pixel 10.
Article Summary: Next-generation video compression technology promises sharper visual quality. Engineering projections indicate that AV2 is roughly 25% to 32% more efficient than its predecessor, AV1. YouTube has confirmed plans to begin rolling out AV2 streaming as early as early 2027, targeting the web browser version of the platform first.

Article Title: Google Brain cofounder and AI pioneer Andrew Ng tells ‘one of the most disgusting things’ he has seen that AI is being used for
Article Text:
‘Balancing AI’s value with dangerous harms’

Artificial intelligence (AI) pioneer and Google Brain co-founder Andrew Ng has spoken out against malicious applications of the technology, noting the generation of non-consensual deepfake intimate photos as one of the most troubling misuses of modern software he has encountered. Addressing the darker side of technological development in an interview on The Economist's "Inside Tech" podcast recently, the Al pioneer dismissed the notion that this technology presents an existential threat to society.Firstly, Ng delivered a strong critique of synthetic explicit content, calling on lawmakers to establish strict regulations and severe measures to eliminate the abuse entirely.“AI applications have problems. For example, one of the most disgusting things I've ever seen is AI being used to generate non-consensual, deepfake intimate imagery,” Ng said, adding, “That's all for the past laws put in place for harsh penalties to just get rid of that.”While acknowledging the severe harms enabled by certain AI deployments, Ng maintained that the broader technology remains enormously valuable. The primary challenge, he indicated, is addressing harmful cases while preserving the societal benefits created by AI. Despite the prevalence of bad actors and misuse, Ng emphasised that he remains optimistic about the future of AI safety governance.“AI is tremendously valuable, but has some problematic use cases.The thing that gives me optimism is that many nations have managed to collaborate on safety issues, even when they disagreed on other things,” he said.To illustrate how the global community can manage safety risks, Ng pointed to commercial aviation as a proven precedent for cross-border collaboration.“For example, airlines around the world actually do not compete on safety and will share safety information because having aviation be safer is a good thing. Even if airlines are competing like crazy for business, I think there's actually room for collaboration,” Ng added.The founder of DeepLearning Al that provides technical training on Generative Al, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and other topics, also alleged some industry leaders of manufacturing existential safety arguments to lobby for regulations that crush open-source competition.
Article Summary: Google Brain co-founder Andrew Ng has spoken out against malicious applications of the technology. Ng noted the generation of non-consensual deepfake intimate photos as one of the most troubling misuses of modern software. The primary challenge, he indicated, is addressing harmful cases while preserving the societal benefits created by AI.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai responds to Sam Altman’s ‘fend Google off’ remark, asks: ‘Are you bolting agents onto ChatGPT, or …’
Article Text:
Flipping the ‘Bolt-On’ question back to OpenAI

Pichai implies ‘winning means both adapting and building new’

Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai has pushed back against claims made by OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman , rejecting the notion that Google is merely retrofitting artificial intelligence (AI) into legacy products rather than developing authentic, AI-first systems. While acknowledging the tough competition, Pichai said that the company has been making AI systems and tools from ground up as well as refining products. The debate stems from comments by Altman regarding competition between the two tech powerhouses, where the OpenAI leader argued that his company builds AI-native applications while implying that Google simply “bolts” machine learning capabilities onto its existing software suite.“First of all, it’s a very dynamic moment. We are all pushing each other. OpenAI has pushed us as a company too. This is not just we are doing something to them. Far from it,” Pichai offered a candid response, emphasising that the intense technological race is driving innovation across the board.“In the AI moment, all of us have to respond with varying levels of urgency at any given moment in time,” he added.Pichai challenged the idea that Google lacks ground-up AI platforms, citing the direct development of the standalone Gemini app as evidence of ground-up product design.He then turned the exact same design critique back toward OpenAI, questioning how ChatGPT itself handles the rapid evolution toward autonomous software agents.“We are constantly building new products as well. Gemini was built from the ground up as a product—the Gemini app I’m talking about,” Pichai noted, asking, “Or tomorrow, as all of us are adapting to agents, are you bolting agents onto ChatGPT, or are they building it natively? How would you think about that? You can always flip these questions back.”Rather than getting trapped in industry labels over what qualifies as “native” versus “integrated,” Pichai explained that successfully navigating the generative AI shift requires deploying both strategies simultaneously. The ultimate goal, he argued, is to deliver standout user experiences that perform and win in the real world.“I don’t think of it that way. I think of it as you want to build world-class product experiences that are AI-native and they are winning. Some of it is adapting products, some of it is rethinking new experiences. They will all be part of how you approach this moment,” Pichai explained.
Article Summary: Pichai implies ‘winning means both adapting and building new’ Google CEO Sundar Pichai has pushed back against claims made by OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman. Altman argued that his company builds AI-native applications while implying that Google simply “bolts” machine learning capabilities onto existing software suite.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang backed a Seattle lab with nearly 7 million GPU hours; its new AI model designs proteins up to 10 times faster and helps tackle pollution
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gives AI computing power nearly 7 million GPU hours to Seattle Lab

The Jensen and Lori Huang Foundation, co-founded by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife Lori recently provided the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design (IPD) with a transformational computing grant totaling nearly 7 million GPU hours. The lab recently introduced RFD4-Proteina, an open, generative model co-developed by IPD and Nvidia. The model is claimed to design proteins up to 10 times faster and uses biomolecular reasoning to improve how well scientists can design new proteins with specific functions.Making RFD4-Proteina open will allow scientists around the world to build on its capabilities, explore more potential protein designs and move promising drug candidates into laboratory testing faster.“RFD4-Proteina will open the door to new solutions in medicine, sustainability, materials and biotechnology,” said David Baker, IPD director and professor of biochemistry at the University of Washington School of Medicine.Earlier this month, the Jensen and Lori Huang Foundation, granted totaling nearly 7 million hours of compute time, will accelerate the IPD’s development of open-source AI models for protein design.The models will enable the creation of molecules with applications in medicine, technology and sustainability.The in-kind grant provided access to graphics processing units. These specialized AI computing systems will cut algorithm learning and evaluation time from months to days. It will help IPD scientists solve complex protein-design problems in such areas as precision cancer therapeutics, durable vaccines, currently untreatable diseases and new enzymes that degrade environmental toxins like long-lasting hazardous chemicals and plastics. The compute power is provided through the Huang Foundation's partnership with CoreWeave using NVIDIA graphics processing units, or GPUs.“Most of the most important medicines of the future will come from proteins that have never existed," said Jensen Huang, co-president of the Huang Foundation. "For David Baker and the Institute for Protein Design, this path means training AI on tens of millions of molecular structures, learning from virtual experiments, and finding novel protein designs that have eluded nature. The Huang Foundation is providing researchers the compute to expand the frontiers of medicine, while ensuring that the resulting models, data, and tools are openly available to all. "
Article Summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gives AI computing power nearly 7 million GPU hours to Seattle Lab. The grant will accelerate the IPD’s development of open-source AI models for protein design. The models will enable the creation of molecules with applications in medicine, technology and sustainability.

Article Title: Apple iPhone Duo scam alert: Fake websites offer 25% discounts to target buyers, Kaspersky warns
Article Text:
iPhone Duo scam alert

Example of a fake website offering to purchase iPhone Duo

Example of a fake multilingual website offering to purchase iPhone Duo

Example of a fake website in Portuguese offering to purchase iPhone Duo

Apple’s first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, has officially gone on sale on October 23, but scammers are already targeting buyers with fake discounts and preorder offers. Cybersecurity firm Kaspersky has identified fraudulent websites in multiple languages that imitate Apple’s style and use limited-time deals to pressure shoppers into sharing personal information. Some sites promise discounts of up to 25%, while others ask buyers to share their contact details or WhatsApp numbers. Kaspersky has warned buyers to be cautious of unofficial offers as they look to get their hands on the new device.These “offers” are not limited to English-speaking audiences. Kaspersky also identified examples of multilingual pages where users can select their preferred language. In one such case, a fake website showcased various features of the new device and invited users to place a preorder, even allowing them to choose the currency for the purchase. To make the offer appear credible, the site suggested that the user would supposedly be redirected to Apple’s official website — which, in reality, is not the case.Kaspersky researchers also uncovered a fraudulent offer aimed at Portuguese-speaking users. In this instance, the scammers tried to move the conversation to a messaging app from the outset, asking the victim to share the phone number linked to their WhatsApp account as well as their email address in order to check product availability.This tactic not only exposes the victim’s contact information, but also leaves them more vulnerable to further social engineering.“Scammers move fast when a flagship device hits the market, because hype creates urgency and urgency lowers caution. These campaigns are designed to look credible, then push the target into a private exchange before they have time to verify anything. For fraudsters, a flagship buyer is a high-value mark: someone already willing to spend big and therefore more likely to share personal or payment-related details. That is exactly why unofficial discounts, preorders, or ‘availability checks’ should be treated as red flags,” says Olga Altukhova, Senior Web Content Analyst at Kaspersky.To shop for a new device without worrying about cyber threats, Kaspersky recommends that users:•Always purchase new products through official and reputable stores to avoid falling victim to fraudulent offers.•Check the authenticity of websites before entering personal data. Double-check URL formats and organizations name spellings.•Use a reliable security solution that detects fraudulent stores and blocks phishing links. To ensure advanced protection against increasingly complex cyber threats, Kaspersky actively amplifies its consumer solutions with AI-powered scam protection – a unified suite of technologies that combines machine learning-based anti-phishing algorithms, real-time behavior monitoring, accompanied by Data Leak and Identity Theft checkers. In 2025, Kaspersky Premium received the "Approved" certification in Fake Shops Detection test by the leading testing lab AV-Comparatives.•Secure your payment information. Use dedicated virtual cards or a dedicated payment service for online purchases to avoid exposing your credit card or bank account information. Store your credentials and financial data in a password manager for secure auto-fill and cross-device synchronization.•Enable multi-factor authentication and monitor accounts: Activate 2FA on IDs and financial apps and regularly review statements for unauthorized activity.
Article Summary: Kaspersky has identified fraudulent websites in multiple languages that imitate Apple’s style. Some sites promise discounts of up to 25%, while others ask buyers to share their contact details or WhatsApp numbers. Kaspersky warns buyers to be cautious of unofficial offers as they look to get their hands on the new device.

“I also want to help people, especially those suffering from life-altering conditions such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and Huntington’s disease.”

A teenager has tested AI chatbots' ability to handle teenage emotions. Ellianna Gu, an eighth-grader from Utah's Salt Lake City, examined responses from OpenAI ’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and Google Gemini. She chose this test after learning that some teenagers were turning to these services for friendship and emotional support. Her project used 84 scenarios involving academic stress, social anxiety, friendship problems, family conflict, loneliness, anger and sadness. Gu found that the chatbots generally produced clear and structured answers, but their replies did not display much empathy. Their performance also changed depending on whether a scenario was written formally or with slang, indicating that writing style could affect the support a teenager received.The project, titledmade Gu a finalist in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. She varied the language in the prompts, including both slang and more formal writing, before submitting all 84 scenarios to ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.She then evaluated the replies using four criteria: empathy, clarity, problem-solving and helpfulness. Most categories were scored on a scale of one to three, while empathy was rated on a scale of one to four.Gu assessed the answers manually and also used AI to analyse them. This allowed her to compare the chatbots’ responses using both human judgment and an automated evaluation.The three chatbots generally provided organised and understandable responses. However, Gu found that their answers often lacked empathy, an important quality when responding to a teenager discussing loneliness, anxiety or another emotional concern. The systems also reacted differently depending on how a prompt was written. A scenario expressed through slang could produce a different response than one describing the same problem in formal language.Their effectiveness scores were also limited. Article Title: Google changes its privacy policy: Your Gmail, Photos data may now be used for ads; what it means for you
Article Text:
Personal Intelligence is what links your Gmail to Google ads

Turning off personalised ads alone won’t stop Gmail data use

Google has reworked a long-standing promise about your inbox. Its updated privacy policy, effective October 16, now allows content from Gmail, Google Photos and Drive to shape the ads you see, as long as you have shared that data with other Google services. The change was first spotted by Android Authority.Until now, the policy carried a plain line saying Google does not show personalised ads based on your Drive, Gmail or Photos content. That line is still there, but it now ends with a qualifier: "unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads." In practice, this covers anyone who has turned on Personal Intelligence, the feature that lets Gemini and AI Mode in Search read from your personal apps.Google pitches Personal Intelligence as a convenience. Ask Search for dinner spots near your hotel, and it can pull the booking from Gmail and suggest restaurants close by. Once connected, that access stretches beyond AI Mode to Discover, Maps, Shopping, Flights, Hotels, Translate and News. The Gemini app has no ads for now, but AI search results already carry sponsored content, and that is where the two meet.Google maintains the feature is entirely opt-in. In a statement, the company said ads will stay relevant to your query, the context of the response and your interests, and "will not be based directly on your Gmail inbox or Photos library."Advertisers cannot see your emails or photos, and your name and email address are not shared with them. Ads built on sensitive categories such as health, religion, race or sexual orientation are still ruled out.Search, however, can still work with summaries and inferences drawn from your emails and photos, and those can feed into what you are shown. Switching off personalised ads in My Ad Center does not stop connected-app data from being used for AI personalisation either.To cut the link, open your Google Account and go to Data & privacy, then Personalisation settings. Select Manage Personalized Recommendations in Search Services, find Connected Content Apps under Additional Personal Intelligence, and disconnect Google Workspace and Google Photos. You can also switch off Personalized Recommendations altogether from the Search Services Personalization page.There is one more step. As Android Authority points out, disconnecting an app does not erase what Google has already stored in Search Services History, even if you delete the original email or photo. That has to be cleared separately from My Activity, or the old data stays tied to your account.
Article Summary: Google has updated its privacy policy to allow personalised ads based on Gmail, Google Photos and Drive content. The change, effective October 16, covers anyone who has turned on Personal Intelligence. Personal Intelligence is what links your Gmail to Google ads. Google maintains the feature is entirely opt-in.

Article Title: Airbnb announces a new ban that goes into effect starting November 20, tells hosts across the world that you cannot make guests complete ...
Article Text:
What Airbnb's new policy says

Airbnb hosts react to the new restrictions

Airbnb also restricts separate contracts

What the changes mean for cleaning fees

Airbnb is introducing new rules for hosts and guests. These new rules restrict the checkout tasks hosts can require guests to complete. The policy, which applies to bookings made on or after November 20, prohibits hosts from asking guests to do cleaning duties typically handled by professional cleaners. These include stripping beds, taking rubbish offsite and washing and putting away dishes.The company has also said hosts cannot bypass the restrictions by moving such instructions to other sections of their listings or providing printed checkout lists. The announcement has triggered criticism from some hosts, who argue that the changes limit their ability to protect their properties, while some travellers have welcomed the move amid longstanding complaints about cleaning fees and checkout chores.According to a WIRED report, Airbnb emailed hosts this week to inform them of the changes. The updated rules prohibit hosts from requiring guests to do tasks a cleaner would normally perform.Airbnb says hosts can still make reasonable demands, such as asking visitors to put dirty dishes in the washbasin. Other authorised directives might require guests to dispose of their trash in bear-proof containers or to save water in places with drought-related limitations.However, hosts cannot require guests to strip beds, wash and put away dishes or take rubbish offsite as a condition of checkout.Airbnb has also restricted attempts to circumvent the rules by placing cleaning instructions in a listing's “Requests” section. In an example shared in a Facebook group for hosts, a user claimed the platform prevented them from saving checkout instructions that included washing dishes, moving dirty towels to a laundry room and taking rubbish to a dumpster.The interface reportedly displayed a message stating, "Guests shouldn't be asked to do this task."Some property owners have criticised the announcement, saying the changes limit their ability to set expectations for guests and protect their homes.“As hosts, we have a responsibility to protect our investments, our homes, and, in many cases, our personal living spaces. The problem is that Airbnb increasingly expects hosts to accept the risks while limiting our ability to protect ourselves,” one person wrote in Airbnb’s official host forum.Another host, posting on Reddit, compared the platform’s approach to an abusive relationship, while some users talked about decluttering their rental kitchens or rethinking hosting altogether.Some hosts have also suggested raising rental prices or temporarily withdrawing listings to protest the changes.A third host took to a Facebook group to write, “Even if we all unlist our properties for just a day or two, we can send a powerful message. Airbnb built its empire on OUR properties. It’s time we reminded them who actually holds the power.”But the policy changes go beyond cleaning instructions. Starting November 20, Airbnb will also ban hosts from forcing guests to sign separate contracts, with certain exceptions.These include situations involving local legal requirements, longer stays or access to optional amenities, such as golf cart rentals. Hosts must disclose applicable requirements in the designated section of their listings.Airbnb has also clarified that it does not enforce these contracts. Hosts who breach the new rules could receive warnings, have their listings removed or, in severe cases, be banned from the platform.The company already has ground rules requiring guests to treat properties responsibly, dispose of rubbish properly and avoid leaving dirty dishes that could become a health concern.The new policy comes amid longstanding complaints from travellers about paying cleaning fees and still being asked to complete checkout chores.Airbnb says cleaning fees cover standard turnover work, including laundry and vacuuming. Hosts cannot charge guests additional fees for failing to complete specific cleaning or checkout tasks, although they can still leave reviews based on cleanliness.The platform’s guest program, AirCover, also covers some types of guest-caused property damage, with eligible claims covered up to $3 million. The program can also cover other cleaning costs, such as removing smoke odours or cleaning up pet accidents.Some hosts say the restrictions could make it harder to keep their properties up to snuff, but travellers are embracing fewer chores, especially as cleaning fees are baked into the price of a reservation.The changes will therefore affect how hosts communicate checkout expectations, with Airbnb drawing a clearer distinction between reasonable requests and cleaning work that guests cannot be required to perform.
Article Summary: Airbnb is introducing new rules for hosts and guests. These new rules restrict the checkout tasks hosts can require guests to complete. The policy, which applies to bookings made on or after November 20, prohibits hosts from asking guests to do cleaning duties. These include stripping beds, taking rubbish offsite and washing and putting away dishes.

Article Title: Experts warn wave of AI-discovered flaws to trigger fresh disruptions in coming months
Article Text:
Weeklong disclosures and ‘fire drills’

Rapid breakthroughs in artificial intelligence (AI) have begun unearthing a stream of hidden software bugs, and cybersecurity leaders warn that the discoveries are certain to trigger waves of disruption in the months ahead. The forecast follows a turbulent week where government agencies and public institutions across Europe, Asia and other regions took government and public portals offline to guard against newly surfaced vulnerabilities in PHP, an open-source programming language that underpins a vast swath of the modern web. Citing multiple cybersecurity professionals, news agency Reuters reported that the episode is just the beginning.Matthew Prince, CEO of cloud and infrastructure giant Cloudflare, confirmed that he is tracking “a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities that are present in other pieces of critical software.” He cautioned that the sector faces an intense operational stretch as algorithmic tools scour the foundational code of the internet for long-buried weak spots.“I think we’re going to have a couple years where every single week it’s going to feel like the sky is falling,” Prince was quoted as saying.The emergency scramble around PHP did not occur in isolation. According to VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity, it coincided with an already present cycle of security disclosures and infrastructure incidents across the tech landscape. Over the same seven-day window critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in Node.js (a popular alternative to PHP) as well as the streaming media platform Plex.Additionally, security breaches surfaced around AI gateway LiteLLM and modern application hosting platform Railway. Revelations emerged that Indian certifying authority eMudhra had relied on an extraordinarily weak cryptographic key, raising potential safety concerns for web users globally.“If we just saw four or five things like this, this week, I would expect we’re going to see a lot more. I think there’s going to be a lot more fire drills for anything that’s internet exposed,” Garrity noted.Modern software platforms rely on massive, sprawling codebases where overlooked flaws can linger for decades.In the past, discovering a complex vulnerability required specialised manual auditing. Engineering a working digital lockpick typically demanded weeks or months of meticulous reverse-engineering by highly skilled researchers. That delay granted security teams a vital buffer window to write, test, and quietly distribute defensive software patches.AI has upended that balance. Autonomous models can continuously audit millions of lines of code, flagging vulnerabilities in succession and synthesising functional exploit payloads in hours.
Article Summary: cybersecurity leaders warn that the discoveries are certain to trigger waves of disruption in the months ahead. The forecast follows a turbulent week where government agencies and public institutions across Europe, Asia and other regions took government and public portals offline to guard against newly surfaced vulnerabilities in PHP.

Article Title: Sigma’s pocket-sized full-frame FP2 launches in India for Rs 2,16,500
Article Text:
Sigma FP2 goes on sale across India on November 11

One switch turns the Sigma FP2 into a cinema camera

Sigma has launched the FP2 in India, a compact full-frame camera priced at Rs 2,16,500 for the body alone. It goes on sale across the country on November 11, and Sigma claims it is the smallest full-frame camera body in the world.The FP2 follows the original fp, which arrived in 2019 as a tiny, box-shaped camera meant to be built up with accessories. The new model keeps that modular idea and pairs it with faster hardware for both stills and video.Inside is a 24.5MP partially stacked CMOS sensor. Sigma says the quicker readout cuts down rolling shutter, the skewed look you get when panning fast on an electronic shutter. Burst shooting reaches about 20fps for up to 200 frames, and autofocus now tracks birds alongside people and animals. There is 70GB of built-in storage next to the SD card slot, so a full card doesn't have to end a shoot. The rear screen tilts 90 degrees up and 45 degrees down, while a dedicated Color button cycles through 13 colour modes.Flip the switch on top and the FP2 reloads its menus, controls and workflow for CINE mode. It records 6K open gate, using the full sensor area so footage can be cropped later for vertical and horizontal platforms.Sigma rates dynamic range at 14.1 stops, with 7 stops of highlight headroom at ISO 1250 and above in 4K full-frame L-Log. ProRes RAW, Leica L-Log, anamorphic desqueeze and 32-bit float audio are all supported. A Director's Viewfinder mode simulates the framing of cinema cameras like the ARRI ALEXA 35 and Sony VENICE 2 and BURANO.Standard 1/4-inch threads let users attach third-party rigs, and Sigma has four new accessories. The EVF-21 viewfinder uses a 5.76M-dot OLED panel, runs off a single USB-C cable and tilts up 90 degrees. The HU-21 hot shoe shares flash communication with OM System and Lumix. There's also the LVF-21 loupe with 2.5x magnification and the BPL-21 base plate for 3/8-inch video gear. Sigma hasn't shared India pricing for these yet.
Article Summary: Sigma FP2 goes on sale across India on November 11 for Rs 2,16,500 for the body alone. It follows the original fp, which arrived in 2019 as a tiny, box-shaped camera meant to be built up with accessories. New model keeps that modular idea and pairs it with faster hardware for both stills and video.

Article Text:
FCC blocks two gadgets over Huawei-linked ‘spy chip’

Why the FCC sees this Huawei camera chip as a surveillance risk

New FCC rule stops blacklisted chips from slipping into other brands’ devices

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has blocked a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter from the American market because they carry chips made by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon. The regulator calls the part a “foreign surveillance chip,” and neither device can now be marketed or sold in the US.This is the first time the agency has used a power it gave itself on October 13. The new rule lets it reject any gadget built around a chip from a company on its national security blacklist. FCC chairman Brendan Carr said such video devices “pose an obvious and unacceptable risk to the nation and our people.”The FCC has not named the brands or models of the two devices. It has, however, singled out HiSilicon’s Hi3516CV610 UHD Smart Vision SoC. This processor takes the raw feed from a camera sensor and turns it into a working home security camera, dashcam or similar device. The agency has not said whether this exact chip sits inside both blocked products.The agency’s case leans heavily on HiSilicon’s own marketing. The company pitches the Hi3516CV610 as a chip made for the surveillance market, with face detection algorithms built in.Its parent, Huawei, has sat on the FCC’s Covered List since March 2021. The list names companies and products Washington considers an unacceptable risk to US national security, and it extends to their subsidiaries and affiliates.The FCC has not said that either device sent data to Huawei. The block rests on who made the chip.The October 13 rule closes what the FCC describes as a component loophole. Earlier, a device assembled and branded by a company not on the list could still win approval, even if a blacklisted firm made the parts doing the actual computing. Now the FCC can block any device using a “logic-bearing hardware component” from a listed company, if the full device would have been barred had that company built it. In plain terms, that covers chips running digital logic at more than 9,000 cycles a second. Passive parts such as housings, wiring, resistors and plain battery cells are left out.The rule has limits. It applies only to new equipment applications, so products already approved can stay on sale. It also covers only companies named on the list, not the country-of-origin bans on foreign-made drones and routers.Online stores get new duties too. Marketplaces will have to show a device’s FCC ID at the point of sale, with deadlines of March 1 and June 1, 2027, depending on how much control a platform has over the product.The block adds to a busy year for Carr’s FCC. Foreign-made routers, power inverters and advanced robots, including robot vacuums, have all been pulled under the Covered List since March. Critics of those moves have asked whether such bans make users safer or mainly decide which manufacturers get to sell in the US. The FCC says it will keep enforcing its component rules aggressively.
Article Summary: FCC blocks a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter. Both carry chips made by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon. The regulator calls the part a ‘foreign surveillance chip,’ and neither device can now be marketed or sold in the US.
